As per prosecution story, minor prosecutrix was travelling by a train from Panjab to Janjgeer with her parents.
She alighted at Jhansi Railway Station to drink water, where the train departed leaving her stranded.

At the station, she was approached by a woman named Rekha (absconding accused),
who falsely promised her to take her home but instant approach her to the house of appellant Banwari at Fatehpur, Shivpuri, where she stayed 15 days doing household chores.

It is also alleged that appellant Banwari took the prosecutrix to accused Sualal at Chakrana, where a team has been initiated to sale her for Rs.60,000/- to the appellant Dharmendra, other co-accused Rambharosi and Devendra.
Prosecutrix was forced into a marriage with appellant Dharmendra at Shivnagar Colony.
She was found in a room and subjected to repeated rape for seven days before her recovery on 28.07.2013.
Accordingly, offence registered at Police Station Pohari, District Shivpuri.

3. Case of prosecution is further that MLC of the prosecutrix has been conducted by Dr. Monika Mangal (PW-5) on 29.07.2013 and she opined that age of the prosecutrix is about 12-13 years and she was subjected to rape.
Her vaginal slide has been prepared and also seized her underwear.
Appellant Dharmendra has also been arrested and his MLC has also been conducted.
Thereafter, all the seized articles have been sent for FSL for its chemical examination.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:7671 3 CRA-365-2014 4.
After completion of investigation, charge-sheet has been filed before the Special Judge under the SC/ST Act.
Prosecution has examined as many as 10 witnesses, while the defence has examined only one witness.
The Trial Court after scrutinizing the entire evidence available on record, convicted and sentenced both the appellants as mentioned hereinabove.
Other co-accused Rambharosi, Devendra and Sualal have been acquitted from all the charges.
Being aggrieved by the impugned judgment and conviction, both the appellants have preferred this criminal appeal.
5. Learned counsel for the appellant Dharmendra has preferred Cr.A. No.365/2014 by stating that the impugned judgment passed by the Trial Court is bad in law.
There is material contradiction in the statement of the prosecutrix and other witnesses.
Ossification test is not conclusive.
The prosecutrix was major at the time of incident.
Prosecutrix has failed to prove her age.
MLC of the prosecutrix has not supported the allegation of rape.
Co- accused Rekha is not traceable yet.
Prosecutrix was not recovered from the possession of appellant Dharmendra.
The Trial Court has committed error in not considering the defence of appellant.
Hence, he prays that the impugned judgment be set aside and appellant Dharmendra be acquitted from all the charges.
6. Learned counsel for the appellant Banwari has preferred Cr.A. No.390/2014 by stating that the entire story of the prosecution appears to be imaginary and hypothetical.
The parents of the prosecutrix never lodged her missing person report.

Prosecutrix travelled with the appellant Dharmendra at different places and lived with him for a considerable period, but she did not Dharmendra Sen vs State Of M.P. on 25 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/110430206/

She was living with appellant Dharmendra after solemnizing her marriage with him.
There is no allegation that the appellant Banwari has committed rape upon the prosecutrix.
Prosecutrix failed to identify the appellant Banwari.
There are material contradictions and omissions in the statement of the prosecution witnesses.
Hence, he prays that the impugned judgment be set aside and appellant Banwari be acquitted from all the charges.
7. Per contra, learned counsel for the State submitted that the impugned judgment passed by the Trial Court is based upon the cogent evidence and proper appreciation of evidence.
The Trial Court has rightly convicted and sentenced both the appellants and same does not call for any interference.

8. Heard the learned counsel for the parties and perused the entire record with due care.
9.
The question which arise for consideration before this Court is firstly, whether the prosecutrix at the time of incident was minor ?
10. Prosecutrix (PW-1) is an illiterate girl.
She categorically stated that her age is about 14 years, but she does not know her date of birth.
Learned counsel for the appellant on the basis of age of other siblings of the prosecutrix contended that the prosecutrix was major at the time of incident.
He refers the relevant portion of the statement of the prosecutrix (PW-1) and her mother (PW-2) and relative (PW-3), but all these witnesses are illiterate persons.
They could not ascertain the date of birth or age of the prosecutrix, therefore, the prosecution has relied upon the ossification test of the prosecutrix.

Dr. Monika Mangal (WP-5), who has conducted the MLC of the NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:7671 5 CRA-365-2014 prosecutrix, opined that the age of the prosecutrix appears to be 12-13 years on the basis of her appearance and secondary sexual characters.

Dr. M.L.
Agrawal (PW-9), who has conducted the ossification test of the prosecutrix, categorically stated that as per the test, age of the prosecutrix has been found between 16-18 years.
11. Learned counsel for the appellant Banwari submits that radiological examination is not a conclusive proof.

In support of his submission, learned counsel has relied upon the judgments passed by Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Mukarrab Vs. State of U.P. reported in (2017) 2 SCC 210 , and Rajak Mohammad Vs. State of Himachal Pradesh reported in (2018) 9 SCC 248.
12.

13. So far as the sexual assault is concerned, prosecutrix (PW-1) categorically stated in her statement that a lady named Rekha, who falsely promised her to take her home, brought her to the house of appellant Banwari, where she stayed for 15 days doing household chores.

Thereafter, appellant Banwari, Devendra and Sualal along with other persons solemnized her marriage with Dharmendra,

14. Prosecutrix (PW-1) categorically stated that she stayed 7 days at the house of appellant Dharmendra and Dharmendra has committed rape upon her four times.

Although the prosecutrix in her cross-examination stated that Dharmendra has done nothing with her private part, but she categorically stated in her further statement that the appellant Dharmendra has put off her clothes and also his own clothes, slept upon her and committed rape upon her.

15. Learned counsel for the appellant Dharmendra contended that in absence of any evidence regarding penetration especially in the instant case, no DNA has been conducted, sole statement of the prosecutrix is not reliable.

He placed reliance upon the judgments of Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Nirmal Premkumar and another Vs. State represented by Inspector of Police reported in (2024) 20 SCC 293, but Dr. Monika Mangal (PW-5) categorically opined that the prosecutrix was subjected to rape.

Although DNA has not been conducted in the instant matter, but the vaginal slide,
underwear of the prosecutrix and semen slide of the appellant Dharmendra have been sent for chemical examination and as per the FSL report (Ex. P-31), semen and human sperms have been found in the vaginal slide as well as underwear of the prosecutrix, therefore, on the basis of FSL report, it is duly proved that the prosecutrix was subjected to rape by the appellant.

Although the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Guddu @ Santosh Vs. State of Madhya Pradesh vide judgment dated 27.4.2006 passed in Criminal Appeal No.1491/2005 has held that - NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:7671 7 CRA-365-2014 "it is not necessary that there should be complete penetration of the penis with emission of semen and rupture of hymen.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Partial penetration within the labia majora of the vulva or pudendum with or without emission of semen is sufficient to constitute the offence of rape as defined in the law.

The depth of penetration is immaterial in an offence punishable under Section 376 IPC."
16.
This citation is completely applicable in the instant case and it has been rightly held by the Trial Court that the prosecutrix was subjected to rape.

17. Now after holding that the prosecutrix was minor at the time of incident and she was subjected to rape, only question, which remains to be decided, is whether the prosecutrix was subjected to rape by the appellant Dharmendra with the help of appellant Banwari ?
18. Minor prosecutrix (PW-1) has been subjected in a detailed cross- examination along with the question and answer.
She categorically deposed that appellant Dharmendra has committed rape with her.

Although she specifically mentioned that appellant Banwari has not committed rape with her, but she stated that Banwari and other 3-4 persons had forcefully solemnized her marriage with Dharmendra and handover her to Dharmendra, thereafter, she has been raped by Dharmendra.
Appellant Banwari had a knowledge that if he will handover the custody of minor prosecutrix to appellant Dharmendra, then he will sexually exploit her.
It indicates the active participation of appellant Banwari in the incident of rape.

19. In the instant case, young girl aged about 15-16 years was left alone NEUTRAL CITATION NO.

Any how, on the false pretext, she was brought to the house of appellant Banwari and thereafter she has been handed over to the appellant Dharmendra.
One can well imagine her trauma after being subjected to such sexual harassment.

On reading of entire evidence of the prosecutrix, the Trial Court has rightly come to the finding that the prosecutrix evidence is cogent and clear to the effect that she has been raped by the appellant Dharmendra.
And Banwari has also played an important role at the time of incident.

Minor prosecutrix was doing household chores in his house and he is having authority to administer upon her as defined in Section 376(c) of IPC.
20.
Learned counsel for the appellant further contended that the prosecutrix has been tutored by her mother and other witnesses.
There are material contradictions and omissions in her statement.
FIR has also been lodged with inordinate delay.
In support of his submission, learned counsel relied upon the judgment passed by the Supreme Court in the case of Thulia Kali Vs. The State of Tamil Nadu reported in (1972) 3 SCC 393.

sentences.text: It is further contended that no report regarding missing person has been lodged in the matter, therefore, sole statement of the prosecutrix cannot be relied upon but from perusal of her statement and other witnesses, it appears that contradictions and omissions in their statements are trivial in nature.

Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Vinod Kumar Vs. State of Haryana reported in (2015) 3 SCC 138 has held that:
"24.................

entities.text: Vinod Kumar Vs. State of Haryana reported in (2015) 3 SCC 138
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is well settled in law that minor discrepancies on trivial matters not touching the core of the case or not going to the root of the matter could not NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:7671 9 CRA-365-2014 result in rejection of the evidence as a whole.

It is also well accepted principle that no true witness can possibly escape from making some discrepant details, but the Court should bear in mind that it is only when discrepancies in the evidence of a witness are so incompatible with the credibility of his version that it would be justified in jettisoning his evidence.

It is expected of the Courts to ignore the discrepancies which do not shed the basic version of the prosecution, for the Court has to call into aid its vast experience of men and matters in different cases to evaluate the entire material on record."

21. On the basis of aforesaid, this Court is of the considered opinion that such contradictions and omissions are trivial in nature and same are neither material nor sufficient to disbelieve the statement of the prosecutrix, which is well supported by other evidence available on record.
Prosecutrix and her family members reside in Janjgeer, Chhattisgarh, which is about 800 km from the District Shivpuri.
Prosecutrix and her mother had no motive to falsely implicate the appellants in the instant case.
22. So far as the delay in lodging the FIR is concerned, it is noteworthy that the minor prosecutrix was also helpless between the accused persons.

When she has been recovered from the possession of Dharmendra Sen vs State Of M.P. on 25 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/110430206/
5 appellant Dharmendra, then matter has been reported to the police, therefore, in view of the facts and circumstances of the case, such delay in lodging the FIR is not fatal to the prosecution.

Ocular testimony of the eyewitness cannot NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:7671 10 CRA-365-2014 be discarded lightly.

(See: State of M.P. Vs. Chakkilal and Another and Ramveer Vs. Chakkilal and Another reported in 2018(4) Crimes 238 SC).
24.

25. Accordingly, both these appeals being devoid of merits deserve to be and are hereby dismissed.
